notes.japanese: 劉の家産も亦とんとん拍子に傾いて
notes.problem: Mistranslates tempo and tone: とんとん拍子に means briskly, in quick succession, not steadily and gradually.
notes.suggestion: His fortune too has tumbled downhill in quick succession — 'steadily' makes the ruin gradual where the Japanese makes it brisk and almost comic.
notes.sureness: Quite sure; any dictionary of とんとん拍子 settles the brisk/rapid sense.

notes.japanese: 険しい顔の骨を包んで
notes.problem: Clarification: 険しい means stern, harsh or haggard, not thin; gaunt adds thinness the text has already given elsewhere.
notes.suggestion: Skin of a poor lustre greasily wraps the bones of a stern face — keep 険しい as stern/haggard rather than interpreting it as gaunt.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; 険しい never means gaunt by itself, though context is emaciation — a dictionary and the surrounding decline passage would settle it.

notes.japanese: 往年の丸丸と肥つてゐた俤
notes.problem: Ennoblement/expansion: sleek adds a gloss not in 丸丸と肥っていた, which is simply roundly fat.
notes.suggestion: no trace remains of the round fat figure of former years — drop sleek to keep Liu's fatness plain as the text has it.
notes.sureness: Quite sure on 丸丸 = round/plump; sleek is the translator's addition, no reference needed beyond the sentence.

data.say: Ending clean on the crux — cure complete, ruin complete, three answers flat and undecided — with only small lexical losses noted.
